doc_screened_files.reason: Best match for the last-wins symptom: this file owns trait candidate evaluation, ambiguity handling, and confirmation, so a bug here could make the later `Table2` impl override `Table1` for the `T::COLUMNS` obligation.
Directly assembles the competing impl candidates for `<T as Table<D>>`; an ordering bug here could explain why the solver picks the `Table2` implementation when both tables are in scope.

The repro is sensitive to the order of the enclosing `where` clauses, and this file is where explicit predicates and const-related bounds are collected into the param environment used by later trait solving.
The failing `where [(); T::COLUMNS]:` constraint is proven through this type-op path, so mis-handling of ambiguous const-evaluatable predicates here could leak the wrong `T` into inference.
This is the query entry point for proving predicates and normalization-backed type ops, so it sits on the path from collected `where` clauses to the solver that mis-infers `T`.

Generic const expressions and anonymous consts rely on this file to determine types from surrounding HIR context, making it a plausible place for the `T::COLUMNS` constraint to be tied to the wrong owner.
The wrong type is reported at the call site in `process_all_tables`, so body type checking is where the bad inference becomes visible and where the callee/obligation interaction is surfaced.
Core inference state underlies the selection of `T` and `D`; if obligation processing overwrites or reuses inference variables incorrectly, the later `Table2` choice could win.
`check_well_formed` appears in the trace, and `generic_const_exprs` adds well-formedness obligations whose processing order can affect which predicate is considered satisfied first.
The problematic `T::COLUMNS` is an associated-item projection, so the projection machinery is a plausible upstream site for the wrong impl/associated-const resolution that feeds the bad inference.
